parsed.explanation: The 2022 Constitutional Court ruling striking down the 'imitating opposite sex' provision is a real, documented traveler-facing positive — criminal exposure for presentation was removed and a court worked for a trans person. But the exposure does not end there: dress-code policing outlasted the ruling with unsourced post-2022 scale, official discrimination persisted a year on, morality laws are strictly enforced, Article 193 (up to 7 years, enforced) remains an active lever against gender-nonconforming people read as same-sex couples, LGBTQ content is regulatorily blocked, films on trans themes are banned, and no protective or community infrastructure exists. Worst documented feature is tier 2–3 (state-tolerated discrimination and enforced morality policing) rather than tier 1: no current universal facility/custody rule, no organised sweeps documented post-ruling, and some functioning judicial recourse. That places it between the unremedied-exposure 0.45 band and partially-mitigated 0.55: above severe/high bands, below jurisdictions with documented acceptance, but not low. Thin post-2022 enforcement data resolves toward the risk the persistent-policing and hostile-climate signals imply, not the midpoint.
